title: Opalite vs. Boostlingo
summary: Compare Opalite Health vs. Boostlingo on AI scribing, EHR integration, and clinical guardrails. An September 2026 guide for CMIOs and ops leaders.
body_markdown:
###


The decision comes down to what your organization was built to do at the point of care. If your primary operational need is scheduling, dispatching, and billing for a large human interpreter network, Boostlingo's management infrastructure fits that workflow. If your priority is AI-first interpretation with multilingual scribing, clinical documentation, and deep EHR integration across eight systems, Opalite Health is the stronger fit for that model.


###


Boostlingo added AI interpretation as a feature layer on top of an existing interpreter management system. Opalite Health was built for the clinical encounter from the start, trained on real clinical conversations and checked through the Opalite Guardian quality framework for medical terminology accuracy, omissions, negation errors, and hallucinations.


###


Opalite Health is designed for hospitals, health systems, FQHCs, and clinics that want AI-first language access with independent clinical validation, multilingual AI scribing, and EHR integration across Epic, Cerner, athenahealth, and five other major systems. Boostlingo is a better fit for organizations whose core need is a dispatch and billing platform for qualified human interpreters, with AI as a secondary capability.


###


Yes. An independent study conducted with Johns Hopkins Medicine found that Opalite produced more than 90% fewer major and critical errors compared with certified medical interpreters in the study. Boostlingo has published research on how AI interpreting should be measured, but has not released a comparable named clinical validation study with a head-to-head comparison against certified interpreters.


###


Boostlingo's athenahealth integration focuses on interpreter session logging, duration tracking, and billing records. Opalite Health produces AI-generated clinical notes from the encounter itself, including SOAP notes, history of present illness, assessment and plan, and after-visit summaries, for provider review before entering the record, and it integrates with athenahealth, Epic, Cerner, eClinicalWorks, and four additional EHRs.


###


Opalite Health is HIPAA compliant and can execute Business Associate Agreements with covered entities. It maintains SOC 2 Type II attestation. PHI is stripped on-device before any cloud transmission; operational and session data (non-PHI) is stored on US-hosted private servers in Ohio. Organizations requiring a security review can request a SOC 2 report, data-flow documentation, and a Business Associate Agreement through Opalite's implementation team.
